 Appearance:
Shri Vishal Sharma - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri S.S.Chawla - Advocate for the respondent.

Order 
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant assailing the impugned award dated 30.08.2010 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 21/2008 whereby an amount of Rs.72,300/- along with interest has been awarded to the appellant/injured.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that meager amount has been awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal in all the heads.

He submits that appellant has suffered grievous injuries, but only Rs.35,300/- has been awarded in the head of medical expenses whereas it should be Rs.40,000/-, in the head of grievous injury, only Rs.25,000/- has been awarded whereas it should be Rs.35,000/-,
no amount has been awarded in the head of pain and suffering, however at least Rs.10,000/- should be awarded in this head.
He further submits that Rs.12,000/- should be awarded for loss of income for four months during the treatment.
On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8529 2 MA-3583-2010 amount.

3. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5 . sentences.text:
grievous injury as assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.25,000/- is on the lower side which needs to be enhanced to Rs.35,000/-, for medical expenses Rs.40,000/- is awarded instead of Rs.35,300/-,
Rs.12,000/- is awarded in the head of loss of income for four months during treatment and also in the head of pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
6. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:

Medical Expenses Rs.40,00  Grievous injury Rs.35,00  Attendant Rs.5,000  Transportation Rs.5,000  Special Diet Rs.5,000  Loss of income for 4 months Rs.12,00  Pain and suffering Rs.10,00  Total: Rs.1,12,
 MACT Awarded: Rs.72,30
Enhanced Amount: Rs.39,70 7 .
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8529 3 MA-3583-2010 Rs.1,12,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.72,300/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.39,700/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate, which was fixed in the impugned award and the other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.

8 . Since this is a case where the learner's licence was there, in the light of the judgment passed in the case of National Insurance Company vs. Swaran Singh 2004 ACJ Page 1 , insurance company cannot be exonerated and maximum principle of pay and recover will be applicable.
